Before you run the installer — the two accounts

The installer does everything it can by itself. Two things only you can do, because they involve agreeing to pay someone: creating the account where your agent's server lives (Hetzner) and the account where its memory lives (Cloudflare). Both take about five minutes. Every screenshot below is from a real first-time run — what you see is what you'll get.

Total cost reality: ~€7/month for the server (hourly billing, delete anytime), €0/month for the memory on Cloudflare's free tier (a payment method on file is required for R2, but 10 GB are free — that's thousands of conversations). Big imported histories may need Workers Paid ($5/month); the installer tells you if yours does.

1. Hetzner — where your agent lives

Create an account at console.hetzner.cloud (needs a payment method — card or PayPal). After sign-up you land here, with a Default project already waiting:

You do NOT create a server yourself — the installer does that. If you already have a server at Hetzner, open the project it is in instead: a token only sees its own project, and the installer can use that server. All it needs is one API token. The whole way in 30 seconds (the clip stops before the token is generated):

The same path as still pictures. In the left sidebar, scroll down to Security:

Inside Security, open the API tokens tab:

You'll see this — click Generate API token:

Name it Embervy, set permissions to Read & Write, generate:

Copy the token immediately — it is shown only once. Paste it into the installer's server step. That's Hetzner done: the installer creates the server, sets it up, and you never touch this console again (except to delete the server if you ever want out — billing stops the same hour).

2. Cloudflare — where your agent's memory lives

Create an account at dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up (email + password, verify the email). The free plan is all you need to start.

Watch it once (23 seconds; nothing is sent in the clip). The box that asks if you are human is yours to tick:

One manual step: enable R2 (the file storage for long-term memory). No API is allowed to agree to billing terms for you — this is the one button only you can press. In the left sidebar find Storage & databases → R2 Object Storage. The whole way in 30 seconds (the clip stops before Activate R2):

The same path as still pictures:

You'll see the subscription page. Note the price: 10 GB/month free, you're only ever charged beyond the free allowance. Click Add R2 subscription to my account (it may ask for a payment method):

The order summary confirms what you're agreeing to — $0/month:

That's it. The installer's Cloudflare step handles everything else through a consent screen you approve once — databases, search indexes, storage, the tunnel, and the worker programs.

And a domain — you need one. The app is how you talk to your agent, and it needs an address: a domain in your Cloudflare account (~€10/year, dashboard → Domain Registration). With one, the installer automatically publishes your agent's app at home.<your-domain> — open it on your phone, add it to the home screen, done. Without a domain you cannot reach your agent at all (unless you know your way around SSH — most people don't, and shouldn't have to).

Only if you bring a chat history: Workers Paid ($5/month). A long history needs more room than the free plan gives; the installer asks about it at the history step. It uses the payment method you added for R2. The way in 30 seconds (the clip stops before Activate):

What you'll have at the end

WhereWhatCost
Hetzneryour agent's server (its "hardware")~€7/month, hourly, cancel anytime
Cloudflarememory (databases, search, archive) + tunnel€0 on free tier
Cloudflarea domain — the app needs an address~€10/year
Cloudflare (only for big history imports)Workers Paid$5/month

Both accounts are yours. The installer never sees your passwords; it works with the one Hetzner token you paste and the Cloudflare consent you approve — and everything it creates is listed in your dashboards, deletable by you at any time. Doors, not cages.
